title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: guided OAuth sign-in for connector admins
summary: The briefing passes: its setup instructions, controls, licensing and roadmap details are supported. Two minor qualifications should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft documentation about editing permissions after creation and federated connector write capabilities.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center connector setup now offers a guided OAuth authentication experience.
claims.quote: Open the Microsoft 365 admin center and start configuring one of the supported connectors. Follow the guided OAuth prompts to complete authentication.

claims.claim: The OAuth setup includes signing in and granting access through a pop-up flow.
claims.quote: Review the workspaces you want to use and the corresponding Microsoft 365 Copilot access level before you choose the install button in the pop-up window.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes effortless authentication unified through OAuth for Connector Admins.
claims.quote: Effortless authentication, unified through OAuth — empowering Connector Admins to connect in just a few clicks. #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: The roadmap description names no individual connectors.
claims.quote: Effortless authentication, unified through OAuth — empowering Connector Admins to connect in just a few clicks. #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: The release notes name Gong, GitHub and Monday as connectors supported by the simplified OAuth experience.
claims.quote: Admins can now set up authentication for Gong, GitHub, and Monday connectors using a simplified, faster OAuth experience.

claims.claim: The release notes say streamlined OAuth replaces lengthy manual connector authentication steps.
claims.quote: The connector setup flow now uses a streamlined OAuth process that replaces lengthy manual steps.

claims.claim: Gong authentication is configured by selecting OAuth 2.0 and then Authorize.

claims.claim: Completing Gong OAuth consent grants the connector access to the required Gong APIs.
claims.quote: Complete the OAuth consent flow to grant the connector access to the required Gong APIs.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance

claims.quote: Enter your organization name. Choose Authorize to sign in and grant access.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: monday.com offers an authentication option named OAuth (recommended).
claims.quote: The monday.com connector supports the following authentication options: OAuth (recommended). OAuth 2.0 with a customized monday.com app.

claims.quote: Install the Microsoft 365 Copilot monday app on your monday Workspaces via this link.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The recommended monday.com authentication flow uses Authorize to sign in and grant access.
claims.quote: Choose Authorize to sign in and grant access.

claims.claim: monday.com also supports OAuth 2.0 with a customized app for organizations requiring their own OAuth configuration.
claims.quote: With OAuth 2.0, you create and configure your own OAuth app in the monday.com Developer Center. Use this option when your organization requires a custom OAuth app configuration.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated an arrival default for this streamlined authentication roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: '502530 default'; 'Copilot streamlined OAuth default'. Read roadmap, February/March release-note entries and Gong, GitHub Cloud Knowledge and monday.com deployment pages; none states this item's arrival default.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not state whether existing connections change or migrate to the guided OAuth method.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Gong GitHub OAuth existing'; 'Copilot connectors OAuth automatically existing'. Read release-note entries and Gong, GitHub Cloud Knowledge and monday.com deployment pages; no migration or reauthorization requirement for existing connections found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The GitHub Cloud Knowledge connector indexes GitHub repository content for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Search.
claims.quote: The GitHub Cloud Knowledge connector enables organizations to index markdown and text files from GitHub repositories into Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Search experiences.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Access Permissions chooses between source-restricted visibility and visibility to everyone.
claims.quote: The Gong Copilot connector supports search permissions visible to Only people with access to this data source (default) or Everyone.

claims.claim: Choosing Everyone can lead to oversharing sensitive content.
claims.quote: Incorrect access permission settings, such as granting access to Everyone, can lead to oversharing of sensitive content.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft says access permissions cannot currently be updated after the connection is created.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.
claims.fix: After the existing statement, add: 'The monday.com deployment page differs: its Customize settings section says default values can be customized after creation and includes Access permissions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/monday-deployment#customize-settings-optional. Retain the manage-access-permissions guidance as attributed guidance rather than silently resolving the disagreement.

claims.claim: The GitHub page marks Customized GitHub app (on behalf of user) as deprecated.
claims.quote: Customized GitHub app (on behalf of user) (deprecated) ... This authentication method is deprecated and isn't recommended for new connections.

claims.claim: The monday.com OAuth consent grants read permissions required for content ingestion.
claims.quote: During authorization, you sign in to monday.com and grant read permissions required for content ingestion.

claims.claim: Federated connectors that can write to source systems are distinct from this synced connector authentication change.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence beginning 'Federated connectors that can write to source systems' to avoid an unnecessary cross-feature documentation conflict: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors still calls federated connectors read-only while also announcing write actions starting early October 2026.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Indexing synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.
claims.quote: Indexing of synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The prerequisites table supports synced connector Copilot grounding and agents with Microsoft 365 plus the Copilot add-on, or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote:
| Microsoft 365 + Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Microsoft 365 E7 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 alone is listed for synced connector Microsoft Search, not Copilot grounding and agents.
claims.quote: | Microsoft 365 (any plan) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |

claims.claim: For organizations with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included without extra charges.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The OAuth setup documentation publishes no separate price or meter for this authentication flow.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Copilot streamlined OAuth connector authentication price billing license'; 'Copilot connectors OAuth pricing'. Read prerequisites/licensing, release-note entries and all three deployment pages; no separate OAuth-flow price or meter found.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Configuring and deploying Copilot connectors requires the AI administrator role in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To configure and deploy Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Prebuilt synced connectors additionally require admin access to the external service.
claims.quote: For prebuilt synced connectors (such as Google Drive, Confluence, ServiceNow), you must have admin access to the external service (Google Workspace Super Admin, Confluence Admin).

claims.claim: The February release-note wording gives examples rather than an exhaustive list of supported connectors.
claims.quote: Complete authentication for supported connectors such as Gong, GitHub, or Monday.

claims.claim: Existing connector staging is edited at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connector > Staged Rollout > Edit.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Find the connector that you want to modify. In the Staged Rollout column, next to Staged, choose Edit.

claims.claim: An API or automation operation for the connector's staged rollout audience is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph Copilot connectors staged rollout limited audience users groups API settings'; 'site:learn.microsoft.com/graph externalConnection staged'. Read staged-rollout and Graph externalConnection references in v1.0/beta; no staging operation found.

claims.claim: A staged rollout accepts up to 100 users.
claims.quote: You can only add up to 100 users and 15 Microsoft 365 groups to the staged rollout list.

claims.claim: A staged rollout accepts up to 15 Microsoft 365 groups.
claims.quote: You can only add up to 100 users and 15 Microsoft 365 groups to the staged rollout list.

claims.claim: The staged rollout audience governs connector data visibility across Search and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Staged rollout settings are applicable to all Search and Copilot experiences.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Tenant-wide user access is managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: An API or automation operation for the tenant-wide Agents User access setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph admin agents settings User access All users No users Specific users groups API'; 'User access plugins API settings'. Read agent-settings, graph-api and Package Management API overview; no operation for this tenant setting found.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: User access offers All users, No users and Specific users or groups for agents and plugins, including connectors.
claims.quote: Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts. ... All users ... No users ... Specific users or groups

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: Connector staging cannot extend access beyond the population allowed by User access.
claims.quote: User access in Agents > Settings covers agents and plugins, including connectors and MCP servers. If it's set to No users or to specific users or groups, connector-level staging can't make a connector available to anyone outside that population.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Access Permissions is reached through Copilot > Connectors > Connectors > Gallery > connector > Custom setup > Users > Access Permissions.
claims.quote: Choose Copilot > Connectors. On the Connectors tab, in the left pane, choose Gallery ... select Custom setup ... On the Users tab, under Access Permissions

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the prebuilt connector's connection-level Access Permissions choice is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph prebuilt synced connector access permissions Everyone Only people with access data source API update'. Read manage-access-permissions, deployment-overview and Graph externalConnection v1.0/beta; no connection-level visibility operation found.

claims.claim: For a new connection, Rollout to limited audience is enabled before Create so only the specified audience sees its data, subject to permissions.
claims.quote: Select the toggle next to Rollout to limited audience. ... Choose Create to create the connection. When the rollout finishes, only the users and groups you specified see connector data in results, depending on their permissions.

claims.claim: Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections shows the connector and its Staged Rollout state.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Find the connector that you want to modify. In the Staged Rollout column, next to Staged, choose Edit.

claims.claim: The Manage access permissions page directs administrators to delete and recreate a connection to correct its visibility choice.
claims.quote: In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection. Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.where: rationale: risk; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The documented default connector access permissions are Only people with access to this data source.
claims.quote: The following table lists the default values that are set. ... Users | Only people with access to this data source

claims.claim: The listed controls govern connector audience or indexed data visibility, rather than authorizing the source-system OAuth step.
claims.quote: Choose an authentication method to access the data source. ... On the Users tab, under Access Permissions, choose whether indexed data is visible to: Only users with access to the content; Everyone in the organization

claims.quote:

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Gong connector indexes calls and meeting-related content for retrieval through Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Search.
claims.quote: Your organization can index calls and meeting-related content like summaries, action items, and call metadata. The connector enables Gong users to retrieve this information through Microsoft 365 Copilot and any Microsoft Search client.

claims.claim: Staged rollout requires the AI administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be an AI administrator to access this feature.

Which users can use agents and plugins, including connectors
Whether indexed connector data is visible to everyone or only people with access to the source
